# Evaluation stack: the runners, the tool layer, the scorer and the analysis.
#
# Everything on this side shares one numpy, and it is the platform's, because the
# tool layer is the component with the hardest constraint (DuckDB, PyArrow and
# XGBoost are built against numpy 2). The serving stack is installed separately
# (requirements-serving.txt) and never shares a virtual environment with it.
#
#     python -m venv .venv-eval && . .venv-eval/bin/activate
#     pip install -r _experiments/env/requirements-eval.txt
#     pip install -r ../STAR-Bench-Web/requirements-tools.txt
#     python -m _experiments.env.check_env
#
# The second line installs the executable AML tools. They are pinned in the
# platform repository so the two copies cannot drift; `check_env` verifies that
# what is installed matches both files and reports any conflict by name.

# Shared with the platform tool layer: these must stay equal to the pins in
# STAR-Bench-Web/requirements-tools.txt. check_env fails when they diverge.
numpy==2.3.5
pandas==2.3.3
scipy==1.18.1

# Model clients. The runner sets max_retries=0 on the client and does its own
# retrying, so the attempt count reaches the run record.
openai==3.14.0

# Scoring
sqlglot==30.18.0

# Analysis and reporting
matplotlib==3.10.7
openpyxl==3.1.5

# Tests
pytest==9.1.1
jinja2==3.1.6

# Optional, for the prompt-budget preflight: with it the check uses the serving
# tokenizer, without it a calibrated byte estimate.
# tokenizers==0.23.1
